best_for: People who keep files in Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive and want them encrypted on their own computer before they upload, without changing cloud provider.

points.title: Encrypts before the cloud sees it
points.text: You create a vault inside your synced folder. Cryptomator encrypts the files on your machine, so the cloud only stores scrambled copies. While unlocked, the vault is mounted so you work with files as usual.

points.title: Desktop is fully free
points.text: Every encryption feature on Windows, macOS and Linux is free and open source under GPLv3. An optional supporter certificate from EUR 29.99 adds dark mode and funds development.

points.title: Mobile write access costs extra
points.text: The iOS and Android apps are free to read vaults, but writing needs a one-time purchase, listed at EUR 29.99. Prices were read on the date below and vary by region.

points.title: Macs work better with FUSE
points.text: Without a FUSE driver, the Mac app mounts vaults over WebDAV. The docs suggest installing macFUSE on Intel Macs or FUSE-T on Apple silicon for a smoother experience.

points.title: Teams use Hub
points.text: Cryptomator Hub manages shared vault access. Community is free, self-hosted, for 5 seats; Standard needs at least 3 seats; Enterprise starts at EUR 10,000 a year for 50 seats.

points.title: Windows MSI for everyone on the PC
points.text: The Windows build is a 64-bit MSI that installs for all users and needs Windows 10 version 1803 or later. The Windows listing keeps 50 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Verified Flatpak on Linux
points.text: The Flathub build is marked verified as published by Skymatic, the company behind Cryptomator, for x64 and Arm64. The docs also offer an AppImage, a PPA and an AUR package.
